definition: Neural modeling field (NMF) is a mathematical framework for machine learning which combines ideas from neural networks, fuzzy logic, and model based recognition.
details: It has also been referred to as modeling fields, modeling fields theory (MFT), Maximum likelihood artificial neural networks (MLANS). This framework has been developed by Leonid Perlovsky at the AFRL. NMF is interpreted as a mathematical description of the mind's mechanisms, including concepts, emotions, instincts, imagination, thinking, and understanding. NMF is a multi-level, hetero-hierarchical system. At each level in NMF there are concept-models encapsulating the knowledge; they generate so-called top-down signals, interacting with input, bottom-up signals. These interactions are governed by dynamic equations, which drive concept-model learning, adaptation, and formation of new concept-models for better correspondence to the input, bottom-up signals.

explainer.lead: Neural modeling field (NMF) is a mathematical framework for machine learning combining neural networks, fuzzy logic, and model-based recognition. It is interpreted as a description of the mind's mechanisms, including concepts and emotions.

tiers.eli5: It's a way to model how the mind organizes knowledge using fuzzy concepts that can adapt, like a flexible filing system.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use NMF for multi-level learning and recognition tasks. A pitfall is that the framework is complex and less widely adopted than standard neural networks.

explainer.example: NMF can be applied to model concept formation in cognitive systems, where concept-models generate and adapt to sensory data.
